pack.title: Money family
pack.description: Decline a financial obligation without debating love.

scenarios.setting: A relative asks you to co-sign a loan you cannot afford to cover.
scenarios.jab: We're family. You should trust me.
scenarios.goal: Decline a financial obligation without debating love.

replies.line: I won't co-sign. It's a financial commitment I can't take on.
replies.why: It explains the kind of obligation you are declining without judging their trustworthiness.
replies.delivery: Pause, then say “I won't co-sign” at a steady, conversational volume. ” then make the financial boundary definite.

replies.why: It gives a clear answer to the specific financial request.
replies.delivery: Say “I can't co-sign the loan” clearly, then stop instead of adding a defense. ” then make the financial boundary definite.

replies.line: I care about you; I can't accept responsibility for this loan, so I won't co-sign.
replies.why: It separates care for the relative from responsibility for the debt.
replies.delivery: Pause after “I care about you,” then make the financial boundary definite.

replies.line: My signature isn't available for financial adventures.
replies.why: The joke concerns your own financial limits rather than the relative's character.
replies.delivery: Keep “My signature isn't available for financial adventures” light; let the joke stand without repeating it. ” then make the financial boundary definite.

followUp.jab: So you don't believe in me?
followUp.line: This is about what I can take on financially; my decision about co-signing is no.
followUp.why: It returns from a test of loyalty to the actual financial commitment.
followUp.delivery: Pause before “This is about what I can take on financially,” keep the volume even, then allow an answer without reopening your decision.
